audiences.description: The line item's `audiences`, projected to `selected[]`, `excluded[]`, and `combine.selected[]`.

buyer_requirements.description: The line item's `buyer_requirements`, projected to `seats` and `seat_owner`.

exclusions.description: The buyer's block lists, keyed by exclusion type. See below

offer.description: The line item and the `version` whose options the figures are computed against. `line_item_id` is REQUIRED here

pricing_id.description: The entry the buyer means to commit under, as `commitment.pricing_id`, so that the figure can count that entry's `unit` (§ 5.6.5)

audiences.description: The line item's `audiences`, projected to `selected[]`, `excluded[]`, and `combine.selected[]`.

buyer_requirements.description: The line item's `buyer_requirements`, projected to `seats` and `seat_owner`.

exclusions.description: The buyer's block lists, keyed by exclusion type. See below

excluded.description: The buyer's write: option ids of options whose `excludable` is `true`, disjoint from the seller audiences in effect. `max_select` does not count them

selected.description: The buyer's choice, by option id. It is the complete set in effect and replaces `included[]`.

seat_owner.description: The legal entity that owns the seats. Absent: the `buyer`

seats.description: The buyer's seats on the deal, as the Deals API 1.0 `wseat`

selected.description: The buyer's choice, by option id. It is the complete set in effect and replaces `included[]`.

value.description: The buyer's value, between the bounds inclusive.

selected.description: The buyer's choice, by option id. It is the complete set in effect and replaces `included[]`.

accountid.description: The account of the advertiser and buyer that own the change, the same as the OpenDirect Order's. An OpenDirect 2.1 ChangeRequest requires it

actor.description: The side that wrote the entry

baseline.description: The agreed line item the request is against, at the `version` of its agreed record (§ 4.1.2). `line_item_id` is REQUIRED here

cancellation.description: The notice, when the request is to cancel under the option in effect (§ 5.6.6)

comments.description: Why the change is requested. Free text

contacts.description: Contacts for this change, in addition to the buyer's and the advertiser's, one per contact type. As OpenDirect 2.1 Contact

id.description: Opaque identifier of the change request

lineid.description: The Line in that Order, for a change at line level

orderid.description: The order the change is requested for: the id in the `order` entry

providerdata.description: Structured references a buyer uses to identify its order in the seller's system

requesterid.description: The organization that requests the change: usually the agency, or the publisher. An OpenDirect 2.1 ChangeRequest requires it

writes.description: The buyer's writes (§ 3.4), keyed by each `line_item_id` that `entry.line_item_ids[]` names

paths.description: The fields the act changed or asked about. MAY be empty

version.description: The version the act created or refers to (§ 4.1.3)

line_item_id.description: The line item. When absent, `pointer` is into the proposal

pointer.description: Into that line item or the proposal

requested_value.description: On a `requested` entry, the value the buyer asked for. On a `declined` entry, or a buyer's `withdrawn` entry, the value of the `request` it ended. Absent on every other entry

held_availability.description: What the hold reserves, as the seller states it on a grant or a re-offer. It can be less than `requested_terms` asks

position.description: Seller-set, 1 for first in line, in the order granted. A later hold moves up only when the one ahead expires, is released or converts. Holds on the same inventory reserve it in that order, so a later hold reserves only what the holds granted ahead of it leave (§ 5.6.1)

reference.description: Seller-set. The seller's id for the reservation, so a buyer can reconcile a hold against the seller's systems

requested_terms.description: The composition the buyer asks to hold, which is not a `commit`. A field it doesn't name reads as § 3.1 and § 3.2 put in effect

valid_until.description: The grant time plus `hold_terms.duration`, or the § 4.3.4 cap if that comes first. With no `duration`, the seller sets it within the cap. It MAY remain on `expired` and `released`

accepted_exclusions.description: What the seller can enforce. See below

activation_route.description: Where the audience is matched. Core terms: `seller_side` (the seller's systems) | `clean_room` (a clean room) | `id_partner` (a third-party identity provider)

addressable_scale.description: What the line item can reach, recomputed against the buyer's selection. Not segment size. See below

agreement.description: The master or annual agreement the line item is priced under. An informative pointer; the agreement itself is outside this specification. A buyer-held agreement id travels as an `external_references[]` entry with `reference_type: agreement`

approval.description: Review SLA and revision policy, in prose

assets.description: A record of the creative that reaches the seller or that the seller builds

availability.description: What the seller says it can deliver, recomputed against the buyer's selection (§ 3.3). See below

billing.description: Who delivers is not always who invoices

break_position.description: Where in the content stream an ad plays, on `video`, `ctv`, and `audio` line items. See 5.2.3. Absent, or nothing in effect: the seller promises no position

cancellation_policy.description: See § 5.6.6. Absent: this field states no right to cancel, and `terms_refs[]` (§ 5.8) may state one

channel.description: Core terms in § 5.1.1. The discriminator for how the rest of the line item is read

commitment_bounds.description: The envelope inside which a buyer may commit, and a buyer MAY request another. See 5.6.1

committed_metrics.description: `CommittedMetric` tuples (§ 5.7.1). Seller declares its offered `level`. A buyer MAY request a stricter `level`, one further in `direction`. A request MUST NOT change a tuple's `direction`

controlling_measurement.description: Whose count of billable units is invoiced. See § 5.7.1. `max_select: 1`. `included[]` MUST name exactly one option

creative_delivery.description: How creative travels. See the creative path below. Absent: this line item states no path, and a `materials_due` still applies

creative_policy.description: Content and category restrictions on creative, in prose

daypart.description: `allowed[]` of `ClockWindow` (below). A window covers any window inside it

deal_origin.description: Absent otherwise. The advertising system domain whose namespace holds the deal ID and that pushes the deal, as the Deals API 1.0 `origin`: typically an SSP, or the ad server for a deal it books itself

delivery_counting.description: How the line item counts plays and, when it counts impressions, turns them into impressions. See 5.6.4

device.description: `allowed[]` of AdCOM 1.0 List: Device Types codes, the values of OpenRTB 2.6 `device.devicetype`. It narrows `environments` (§ 5.2.1). Mobile/Tablet - General (1) covers Phone (4) and Tablet (5)

eligible_buyers.description: The buyers that may commit, by `buyer.domain`

eligible_seats.description: The seats that may commit. An entry with an absent or empty `ids[]` names no seat and admits no one, unlike an absent OpenRTB 2.6 `Deal.wseat`, which sets no restriction

environments.description: The distribution channels and device types the line item runs on. See 5.2.1. Absent: the seller promises no environment

episodes.description: `new` | `catalog` | `all`. `new`: released within the flight. `catalog`: released before it. `all`: either

exclusions.description: The buyer's block lists, keyed by exclusion type. See below

exclusivity.description: See § 5.6.7. Nothing in effect: no exclusivity

external_references.description: The ids other systems hold for this line item. The party that learns an id writes the entry. Once the deal exists in `deal_origin`, the seller MUST record its ID as one `deal` entry on the line item. An entry is not a term and MAY be added after `agreed`

formats.description: Format ids, such as `display/300x250` and `audio/host-read-30s`. Absent: this line item states no format

geo.description: Where the line item runs. `allowed[]` of `GeoCode` (below). A line item MUST NOT declare both `geo` and `markets`

hold.description: The buyer's hold. Absent until the buyer first asks. See 5.6.2

hold_terms.description: Offers a hold. Absent means `available` is `false`. See 5.6.2

markets.description: For a line item priced by market. See `GeoCode` below

materials_due.description: Deadline for creative to reach the seller. A buyer MAY request a later date

measurement_source.description: Lets a buyer choose the measurement provider it transacts on. See § 5.7.1. Nothing in effect: no provider

placement.description: What every impression of this line item is: rewarded, interstitial, video placement subtype, skippability, playback, API frameworks, refresh, server-side insertion and audio feed. See 5.2.2

preemption.description: See § 5.6.7. Absent: no later sale preempts this line item

production.description: Custom units. See `ProductionOption` below. Nothing in effect: no custom unit

programs.description: The content the line item serves within. See 5.2.9. Absent, or nothing in effect: no content is promised

properties.description: What the line item runs on. See 5.2.4. Absent: the seller promises no property

renewal_right.description: The current advertiser's right to the next cycle. Core term: `first_refusal`, the right to buy the next cycle before it opens up. Absent: no such right. It is not a place in a hold queue (`hold.position`)

reporting.description: See § 5.7.1. Nothing in effect: no report is promised

required_credentials.description: What a buyer holds to be eligible

retention.description: From release or air. The ad stays in every copy of the content the seller distributes for at least `min` and is removed by `max`. No `max`: indefinitely. When `placement.feed` is present, only copies in that feed count toward delivery

serving_mode.description: How the ad reaches the content or the player. Core terms: `dai` | `scheduled` | `embedded`, defined below. `placement.ssai` states server-side insertion

serving_platform.description: The ad platform that serves the line item, such as the seller's ad server, by its domain. For a deal sold through a separate SSP it differs from `deal_origin`

shortfall_remedy.description: Core terms: `makegood` | `credit` | `none`. See `remedy_terms` in § 5.7.1. Nothing in effect: this line item states no remedy. Its committed levels stay guaranteed, because only `none` makes them targets

sov_basis.description: `impressions` | `loop_time`. `impressions`: a share of the line item's eligible impressions (digital placements, pooled DOOH products). `loop_time`: a share of each named screen's loop time (fixed-loop DOOH spots)

sov_share.description: Absent under `loop_time`. The promised share, greater than 0

status.description: Independent of the proposal's status, so one line item may sell out while the rest of the shelf stays live

terms_refs.description: The binding documents of this line item, such as a main agreement and its addenda, or an IO template. Every entry applies, with no AND or OR. A `commitment` entry accepts them all (§ 4.1.2). Absent: a `commitment` entry accepts no document

time_zone.description: The clock for `daypart` and a calendar `frequency_cap.period`

transaction_mechanism.description: The mechanisms the seller offers. A seller MAY offer the same inventory through more than one. `max_select: 1`

addressable_scale.description: What the line item can reach, recomputed against the buyer's selection. Not segment size. See below

audiences.description: The line item's `audiences`, projected to `available[].id` and `available[].name`.

break_position.description: The line item's `break_position`, projected to `available[].id`, `available[].delay`, and `available[].slotinpod`.

channel.description: Core terms in § 5.1.1. The discriminator for how the rest of the line item is read

commitment_bounds.description: The envelope inside which a buyer may commit, and a buyer MAY request another. See 5.6.1

committed_metrics.description: `CommittedMetric` tuples (§ 5.7.1). Seller declares its offered `level`. A buyer MAY request a stricter `level`, one further in `direction`. A request MUST NOT change a tuple's `direction`

delivery_counting.description: The line item's `delivery_counting`, projected to `impression_multiplier.impression_type`, `impression_multiplier.source_type`, and `impression_multiplier.accreditation`.

episodes.description: `new` | `catalog` | `all`. `new`: released within the flight. `catalog`: released before it. `all`: either

geo.description: Where the line item runs. `allowed[]` of `GeoCode` (below). A line item MUST NOT declare both `geo` and `markets`

markets.description: For a line item priced by market. See `GeoCode` below

placement.description: The line item's `placement`, projected to `reward`, `instl`, `plcmt`, `skip`, and `feed`.

pricing.description: The line item's `pricing[]`, each entry projected to `pricing_id`, `cost_method`, `list_rate`, `currency`, `price_type`, and `unit_bounds`.

programs.description: The line item's `programs`, projected to `available[].id` and `available[].content`.

properties.description: The line item's `properties`, projected to `available[].id`, `available[].name`, `available[].domains[]`, `available[].apps[].store`, `available[].apps[].bundle`, `available[].child_audience`, `available[].seller_relationship`, and `available[].venue_type`.

required_credentials.description: What a buyer holds to be eligible

store.description: The app store that issued `bundle`. Core terms: `apple_app_store` | `google_play` | `roku_channel_store` | `amazon_appstore` | `samsung_apps_tv`. A `bundle` is unique only within its store. No OpenRTB equivalent

available.description: The line item's `audiences.available[]`, each entry projected to `id` and `name`.

delay.description: A value from List: Start Delay Modes, such as Pre-Roll (0)

slotinpod.description: A value from List: Slot Position in Pod

available.description: The line item's `break_position.available[]`, each entry projected to `id`, `delay`, and `slotinpod`.

allowed_dsps.description: The DSPs that may receive the deal (§ 5.8), each by its primary domain, as `SeatRef.dsp` (§ 2.2)

impression_multiplier.description: The line item's `delivery_counting.impression_multiplier`, projected to `impression_type`, `source_type`, and `accreditation`.

included.description: The options in the base rate, by option id.

accreditation.description: The standing of the multiplier's source in the market. Core terms: `industry_currency` (the market's joint industry currency, such as Geopath in the US or Route in the UK) | `publisher_reported` (the publisher's own figure). A receiver that doesn't know a term reads the multiplier without it

impression_type.description: `gross` | `viewable` | `lts` | `audience`: Gross, Viewable (OTS), Likelihood-to-See, or Audience impressions, as the MRC Out-of-Home Measurement Standards (Phase 1 & 2 Combined, December 2025) define them

source_type.description: Who supplies the multiplier. A value from AdCOM 1.0 List: DOOH Multiplier Measurement Source Types other than Unknown (`0`), such as Publisher Provided (`2`). The value OpenRTB 2.6 `imp.qty.sourcetype` carries

feed.description: A value from List: Feed Types, such as Podcast (3)

instl.description: The ad is interstitial or full screen

plcmt.description: A value from List: Plcmt Subtypes - Video, such as Instream (1). Its presence states that the line item is video, so a `ctv` line item that sells video carries it

reward.description: The user receives a reward for viewing the ad

skip.description: Video or audio. The placement lets the user skip the ad

cost_method.description: The billable unit. Core terms in § 5.6.5

currency.description: The currency of the entry's rates (below)

list_rate.description: The rate before options. A buyer MAY request another value, and a granted value is the `list_rate` of the next `version`

price_type.description: How `agreed_rate` clears, as Deals API 1.0 `terms.pricetype`: Dynamic (0), the auction type of each bid request; First Price (1); Second Price Plus (2); Fixed Price (3); or an exchange-specific value, 500 and up

pricing_id.description: Names the entry within the line item. A revision MUST NOT reuse it for a different `cost_method`, `cost_parameters`, `currency`, or `transaction_mechanisms[]`

unit_bounds.description: Bounds on the units committed under this entry, counted in its unit (§ 5.6.5): `commitment.amount` when `basis` is `units`, otherwise `derived_units`. A buyer MAY request another. Absent on a `FLAT` entry

id.description: Option id (§ 3.1). It is not compared with delivered content

available.description: The line item's `programs.available[]`, each entry projected to `id` and `content`.
The line item's `properties.available[]`, each entry projected to `id`, `name`, `domains[]`, `apps[].store`, `apps[].bundle`, `child_audience`, `seller_relationship`, and `venue_type`.

apps.description: The line item's `properties.available.apps[]`, each entry projected to `store` and `bundle`.

child_audience.description: `directed` | `mixed` | `general`. `directed`: children are its primary audience under the law the seller applies, or its app store lists it for children only. `mixed`: directed to children but not as its primary audience, or listed for children and older users. `general`: neither. § 5.2.7 states what follows

domains.description: The property's domains. On a `dooh` line item, the inventory owner's domain, as OpenRTB 2.6 `dooh.domain`

venue_type.description: `taxonomy` is a value of AdCOM 1.0 List: DOOH Venue Taxonomies. `ids[]` holds exactly one id. It covers only itself, not its descendants. The values OpenRTB 2.6 `dooh.venuetypetax` and `dooh.venuetype` carry

audiences.description: The line item's `audiences`, projected to `selected[]`, `excluded[]`, and `combine.selected[]`.

buyer_requirements.description: The line item's `buyer_requirements`, projected to `seats` and `seat_owner`.

exclusions.description: The buyer's block lists, keyed by exclusion type. See below

description.description: Prose, not a name. Where the "why buy" case is made, including which channels a multi-channel proposal spans

full_url.description: Where the second phase fetches the Full Representation

line_items.description: The full form's line items, each as a summary. In a manifest entry, only those § 2.3 lists

offer_window.description: The window the offer holds: it does not hold before `start` or after `end`. This is the offer window, not the campaign flight

packages.description: The full form's packages, each as a summary. In a manifest entry, only those § 2.3 lists

version.description: Monotonically increasing revision number, starting at 1, held by the seller. Each version is a snapshot of the proposal's offered terms (§ 4.1.3). A version is frozen at the earliest of: the proposal's `status` leaving `draft`; a `negotiation_history[]` or `assent[]` entry naming it; a counterparty receiving it in any representation (§ 2.1). The offered terms of a frozen version MUST NOT change; a change to them creates version `n+1`. The values § 4.1.3 lists as not offered terms change without a new version

add_ons.description: Line items sold only with all of `line_items[]`, such as a bonus line item (§ 5.6.3)

line_items.description: The line items sold only together. It holds at least one entry

min_commitments.description: Thresholds a `commit` meets to include an add-on

add_ons.description: Its `add_ons[]`, each as a summary. In a manifest entry, only those § 2.3 lists

assent.description: The parties' acts (§ 4.1.2). Each entry is written whole by the party its `role` implies. Entries MUST NOT be edited or removed

best_for.description: Advisory planning hints. Non-normative, and never the basis for a match

brief_id.description: The buyer's brief this proposal answers

buyer.description: The entity that assents, usually the agency. Its presence makes the proposal issued to that buyer (§ 4.3). Whom the spend is for is `commitment.advertisers[]` (§ 5.6.1), and whether the buyer may bind that advertiser is authorization (§ 1.2). `legal_name` is REQUIRED here

change_requests.description: Ordered post-`agreed` history. Each entry carries the fields of the OpenDirect 2.1 ChangeRequest, except its `webhook`, plus `baseline`, `actor`, `at`, and `cancellation`. Outside the binding record (§ 4.1.1) and the offered terms (§ 4.1.3), like `negotiation_history[]`, so an entry changes neither `record_digest` nor `version`

description.description: Prose, not a name. Where the "why buy" case is made, including which channels a multi-channel proposal spans

issued_from.description: The shared proposal and version an issued proposal was made from (§ 4.3). A pointer: nothing is inherited through it

line_items.description: The line items (§ 5), in the order the seller wrote them. A proposal holds `line_items[]` or `packages[]`, not both

negotiation_history.description: Ordered, append-only. Entries MUST NOT be edited or removed. A commit and its answers are in `assent[]`, not here, and an entry here voids nothing

offer_window.description: The window the offer holds: it does not hold before `start` or after `end`. This is the offer window, not the campaign flight

packages.description: The line items in packages (§ 4.1.4), in the order the seller wrote them

proposal_template_id.description: Links a proposal to the seller's template. Opaque to buyers; used for the seller's reporting

seller.description: The selling entity. `seller.domain` is the seller's identifier for all purposes, including `assent[]`. `legal_name` is REQUIRED here

spec_version.description: The version of this specification the document follows, such as `3.0`

version.description: Monotonically increasing revision number, starting at 1, held by the seller. Each version is a snapshot of the proposal's offered terms (§ 4.1.3). A version is frozen at the earliest of: the proposal's `status` leaving `draft`; a `negotiation_history[]` or `assent[]` entry naming it; a counterparty receiving it in any representation (§ 2.1). The offered terms of a frozen version MUST NOT change; a change to them creates version `n+1`. The values § 4.1.3 lists as not offered terms change without a new version

generated_at.description: When the seller generated the file

hold_limits.description: The most holds (§ 5.6.2) the seller grants at once across its line items

spec_version.description: The version of this specification the file follows

description.description: Prose, not a name. Where the "why buy" case is made, including which channels a multi-channel proposal spans

line_items.description: The full form's line items, each as a summary. In a manifest entry, only those § 2.3 lists

offer_window.description: The window the offer holds: it does not hold before `start` or after `end`. This is the offer window, not the campaign flight

packages.description: The full form's packages, each as a summary. In a manifest entry, only those § 2.3 lists

version.description: Monotonically increasing revision number, starting at 1, held by the seller. Each version is a snapshot of the proposal's offered terms (§ 4.1.3). A version is frozen at the earliest of: the proposal's `status` leaving `draft`; a `negotiation_history[]` or `assent[]` entry naming it; a counterparty receiving it in any representation (§ 2.1). The offered terms of a frozen version MUST NOT change; a change to them creates version `n+1`. The values § 4.1.3 lists as not offered terms change without a new version

legal_name.description: The party's legal name. A `registry_id` entry that applies can attest it; the value alone attests nothing

description: The OpenProposal composition: the documents and profiles, and every type that composes the modules' types, each defined once; each document's file is a reference to its definition here.
